label: Indexer node operational state
type: enum. The state of the Index Service ON ONE NODE - not of an index. Surfaced as the `status`/`Status` field of an index in the UI and REST view, because an index's reported status is read from whichever node stores it
supersedes: concepts/capella/index-ui-status.json (deleted in round 16 - see the fold below)
recurrence_note: Three files across two product trees, after the round-16 fold. ONE OF THE THREE QUOTES IN THE CORPUS IS DEFECTIVE - stated here as a correction rather than silently repaired upstream. The server manage-indexes.md relation cites 'status. The current state of the Index Service on the node on which this index is stored. ...', which is unquotable: the page writes '* **status**. The current state ...'. The emphasis markers were dropped, and nothing but candidate-evidence.py --audit would have caught it, because the sentence is otherwise word-perfect and the meaning unchanged. That is the second defect shape of this kind found in the POC (the first: a quote assembled from two real fragments joined by a literal '...'), and both are failures of TRANSCRIPTION, not of comprehension - which is why they survive review by a reader and not comparison against the file. The other two quotes are exact.
note:
PROMOTED AS AN ENUM, AND THE ROUND'S CLEAREST FOLD: this record merges what was promoted in round 12 as capella:index-ui-status, whose file is deleted. The merge licence is the strongest kind the POC recognises - the same defining sentence on a page in each tree, differing by one word:
  server/7.2/manage/manage-indexes/manage-indexes.md: '* **status**. The current state of the Index Service on the node on which this index is stored. The state can be expressed as **ready**, **pause**, **warmup**, or **n mutations remaining** (where **n** is an integer).'
  cloud/clusters/index-service/manage-indexes.md: 'Status | The current state of the Index Service on the node where this index is stored. The possible statuses include **ready**, **pause**, or **warmup**.'
WHY THE JOIN WAS MISSED FOR FOUR ROUNDS, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON. The round-12 agent did compare its new enum against the registry and refused to merge it with index-state, correctly and in writing: 'a value set (ready/pause/warmup) that does NOT match the existing index-state enum's values ... Kept as a distinct concept rather than merged, since no page reconciles the two vocabularies.' That refusal was right about index-state and blind to index:indexer-node-state, which was already in the corpus with the same three values - because it had never been promoted, so registry-digest.py could not show it. The agent searched the registry; the id it needed was in the extraction layer. A REFUSAL IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE SET IT SEARCHED, and a registry digest is the wrong set for 'has anyone named this already?'. This is the second time a well-argued refusal has been overturned by evidence that was already on disk (see index-type:hyperscale-vector's note for the first).
DISTINGUISH FROM index-state, and note it is genuinely a different thing rather than a different spelling: index-state (scheduled for creation / deferred / building / pending / online / offline / abridged) is the lifecycle of AN INDEX, from the SQL++ DDL reference; this is the condition of A NODE'S INDEX SERVICE. Round 12's refusal to merge those two stands and is reaffirmed here. The value 'n mutations remaining' is not a state name but a state TEMPLATE carrying a number, which is why this is an enum with a documented irregular member rather than a closed value list; the Capella table omits it - see docs-issues/server-indexer-status-enum-value-sets-differ.
A THIRD VOCABULARY IS NOT PROMOTED AND IS THE ROUND'S OTHER STATE FINDING: server/7.2/learn/services-and-indexes/indexes/storage-modes.md uses two more state words in two sentences, at two different levels, without naming either scheme - 'the indexer goes into the Paused mode on that node; and although the indexes remain in `Active` state, traffic is routed away from the node' (node level, plus 'the indexer goes into Active mode again on that node' in the next paragraph) and 'these indexes remain in the `Warmup` state until all information has been read into memory: then, final updates are made with the indexes in `Active` state' (index level). `Active` appears in NEITHER promoted enum, and `Warmup` is a NODE state here while that sentence applies it to an INDEX. Whether 'ready' and 'Active' name the same state is exactly the kind of thing a source must say and none does, so they are left unmerged - see docs-issues/server-index-state-vocabularies-inconsistent. The 8.0 rewrite of that page (server/current/indexes/storage-modes.md) splits the Paused sentence in two - 'the indexer goes into the Paused mode on that node. Although the indexes remain in `Active` state, traffic is routed away from the node.' - so the quote above is the 7.2/7.6 wording specifically. Both state words survive the rewrite; neither gains a definition.
relates_to_competency_question: What state is this index in, and is that a fact about the index or about its node?
